newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarians allowed to buy OECD bonds from Jan 1.
newsitem.headline: Hungarians allowed to buy OECD bonds from Jan 1.

text.p: Hungarians will no longer need permission from January 1 to buy OECD member countries' government and corporate bonds with at least investment grade and a maturity of at least one year, the government said Thursday.
The government said in a statement that the measure continues Hungary's liberalisation of foreign currency deals.
Hungary joined the Paris-based Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development in March.
"Portfolio investments opportunities for Hungarians will expand further," the statement said.
These securities will also be allowed to enter Hungary's capital markets.

Currently Hungarians are only allowed to buy without a licence from the National Bank of Hungary OECD members' government bonds and the stocks or bonds of AAA-rated companies registered in any OECD countries.
Hungary will also abolish on January 1 all limitations on foreign currency purchases by Hungarian private citizens, the statement added.
Currently each citizen may buy foreign currency up to the equivalent of 1250 SDRs before each journey abroad.
